en.headline: Italy approves decree to lower electricity bills
en.subheadline: The new Decreto Bollette sets a gas price cap and a refund mechanism to ease household costs.

body.text: The Council of Ministers approved the new Decreto Bollette, the government announced on 9 November.
The decree triggers a safeguard when gas prices rise above €58.9 per megawattora, preventing the full increase from being passed to electricity rates.
From January, the measures are expected to cut the average electricity price by about €15 per megawattora, according to the environment minister.
The law provides a temporary reduction through a refund of the natural‑gas cost component used in thermal power generation.

why_it_matters.text: If the gas‑price cap and refund mechanism work as described, households and businesses could see lower energy bills, easing the impact of high energy costs.

key_facts.text: Gas price trigger set at €58.9 per megawattora
Average reduction projected at €15 per megawattora from January

A partire da gennaio, le misure dovrebbero consentire una riduzione media di circa 15 euro al megawattora, secondo il ministro dell’Ambiente.
Il provvedimento prevede una riduzione temporanea del costo dell’energia elettrica attraverso un rimborso della quota di gas naturale impiegata nella produzione termoelettrica.
